Retaining wall questions to settle early Permit, cost and material answers depend on the property and complete wall system. Do I need a building permit for a retaining wall in Victoria? A building permit is required for a retaining wall 1 metre or more high. A lower wall may still require one when it is associated with other building work or protects adjoining property. A registered building surveyor should assess the site. Could a planning permit also be required? Yes. Planning overlays, zoning, easements and title restrictions are separate from the building-permit question. Check the property-specific controls before work begins. Does a wall near a boundary need extra checks? Yes. Even below 1 metre, a wall can require a permit where excavation or retention could damage adjoining property. Boundary location and protection work should be reviewed before digging. Can a retaining wall be built over an easement? An easement can restrict construction and access to services. Check the title and obtain any required authority or council consent before fixing the wall alignment. Bring the site facts together Ready to describe your retaining wall project?
